newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Santos port launches program to improve efficiency.
newsitem.headline: Santos port launches program to improve efficiency.

text.p: Brazil's key port of Santos has been selected for a pilot project to improve efficiency and speed the movement of merchandise which if successful could be imposed nationwide, the port authority Codesp said.

"We had a meeting with the officials of Gempo, which is the executive in charge of port modernisation, at which commissions were formed and the pilot program was launched on Feb 24," a spokesman for Codesp said.
"The aim is to decongest the port and to improve the transit speed of the merchandise, and also for some of these bureaucratic measures to cease to exist," he said.
The meeting included members of the Codesp board, portworkers and union officials as well as high-level officials from Santos port and Gempo, the statement said.

Details of the commissions, which will include representatives from the Ministries of Health, Justice, Finance, Transport and Industry, Agriculture and Supply, Commerce and Tourism and the Navy, will be announced on Feb 27.
The so-called harmonisation plan could also help avoid or shorten strikes, the spokesman added. "Certainly (it will help) because the Labour Ministry is also involved," he said.
The launch of the program coincided with a one-day strike by warehouse workers on Monday over a dispute on backpay.

Santos was chosen because of "the nature and volume of its shipments, the feeling that there is a great predisposition towards harmony and the certainty that...Santos can pave the way for the country's other ports," the statement said.
The initial duration of the project will be three months and it could become a presidential decree, officials said.
